title: What San Francisco public bodies pay federal lobbyists
question: How much public money goes to lobbyists in Washington, and do the lobbyists' own reports agree with the City ledger?
finding: San Francisco public bodies have paid federal lobbyists $17.9 million since 2014 by the lobbyists' own reports, $11.6 million of it from the City, the airport and the water utility. The two records broadly agree: the firms reported $8.8 million from those three for 2017 to 2025, and the City ledger shows $9.2 million paid to the same firms in fiscal years 2017 to 2026, which also covers any other work they did.
how: Lobbyists must report each quarter what a client paid them. Every report naming a San Francisco public body was added up by body, firm and year (an amendment replaces the original). The City ledger total is every payment to a vendor of the same name. Reported political gifts are the firm's own and its lobbyists' federal contributions on their twice-yearly LD-203 reports, counted once per line.
limits: Hiring a federal lobbyist is common for cities. Lobbying income is rounded to the nearest $10,000 by rule and reported by calendar quarter; the ledger is by City fiscal year and includes legal or other work by the same firm, so the two should be close, not equal. BART, the Transbay authority, the transportation authority and City College keep their own books and are not in the City ledger. A firm's political gifts are its own and are not tied to any client.
